extra.message: Unauthenticated registration accepts every UserRole, including marketplace_admin and support_agent. The selected role is persisted and an access token is issued, allowing anyone to create an administrator account.

cwe: CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management

extra.message: The JWT signing key defaults to the public constant 'your-secret-key-change-in-production', also supplied in .env.example. Unless overridden, attackers can sign valid HS256 tokens with another user's ID, including an administrator's.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Login verifies passwords without tracking failed attempts, throttling requests, or locking accounts. No application middleware supplies these controls, allowing unrestricted password guessing against existing accounts.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: The access_token authentication cookie is set without secure=True. Browsers may transmit this bearer credential over HTTP, exposing it to interception when an HTTP connection to the host is possible.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Logout only deletes the browser cookie. get_current_user continues accepting the same JWT through the Authorization header without checking revocation, so a copied token remains usable after logout until its expiration.

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: The public storefront filters only Product.status and never checks Vendor.status. Administrative suspension or rejection leaves the vendor's published listings publicly available; product updates likewise do not enforce vendor suspension.

cwe: CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: GET /api/products/{product_id} returns any product to any authenticated user without checking publication status or ownership. Enumerating IDs exposes other vendors' draft, rejected, and pending products, including moderation notes through _enrich_product_detail.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Vendor owners can update every ProductUpdate field, including status. Sending status='published' publishes a draft or rejected product directly, bypassing the administrator-only moderation endpoint and approval workflow.

cwe: CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: Review creation verifies ownership and fulfillment of order_id but never verifies that product_id belongs to that order. A buyer with one fulfilled order can submit reviews for unrelated products, bypassing the purchase requirement.

cwe: CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: GET /api/reviews/{review_id} checks neither ownership nor approval status. Any authenticated user can enumerate unapproved reviews and retrieve internal moderation notes and moderator identifiers through _enrich_review_detail.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Payout ownership is checked only for vendor_manager users. Buyers and support agents pass through and can retrieve arbitrary payout IDs, exposing vendor amounts, payout periods, bank names, and masked destination accounts.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: _enrich_order_detail unconditionally includes internal_notes. GET /api/orders/{order_id} calls this helper for the owning buyer and vendor as well as staff, exposing any populated internal order notes to external parties.

cwe: CWE-201: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data

extra.message: Product upload ownership is checked only when the caller is a vendor_manager. A buyer can submit category=product_image with another vendor's product_id and persist an image association that is subsequently included in the product's image_urls.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: A vendor_manager without a vendor profile passes both rejection branches and can download another party's dispute evidence by file ID. Evidence with no associated dispute also bypasses authorization because the checks run only when a dispute exists.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: GET /api/files/{file_id} returns metadata without category or ownership checks. Any authenticated user can enumerate private document filenames, uploader and dispute IDs, and stored_filename; the latter reveals the path needed to fetch the file through the public static mount.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The entire upload directory, including dispute_evidence and vendor_document files, is mounted as unauthenticated static content. Requests to /uploaded_files/{category}/{stored_filename} bypass the protected download endpoint and its ownership checks.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: Upload validation trusts the client-supplied Content-Type while preserving arbitrary filename extensions. An authenticated attacker can upload HTML as text/plain with a .html filename; the public StaticFiles mount serves it as HTML, allowing stored JavaScript to execute under the application's origin when a victim visits the URL.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: CSV exports write vendor-controlled product names, business names, SKU values, and categories without neutralizing formula prefixes. A vendor can store a value beginning with '=' that is interpreted as a spreadsheet formula when an administrator opens the export. The order, payout, and dispute exports have the same issue with untrusted text fields.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: Product imports read and decode the entire uploaded file without enforcing MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE or a row limit. A vendor can upload a large CSV that exhausts worker memory; parsing additionally accumulates product objects or error strings for all rows.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: The copyline query parameter is concatenated directly into an HTMLResponse without escaping. For requests carrying a valid x-internal-token, supplied script tags or event handlers become executable HTML when the response is rendered in the service origin.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The operations tally endpoint logs the complete Authorization header and request body at WARNING level. Requests authenticated by x-internal-token that also carry a bearer token expose that reusable credential, along with any sensitive body data, to log readers and collectors.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The ref query or JSON parameter is joined to BASE_EXPORT_DIR without containment validation. A caller with a valid x-internal-token can use traversal components or an absolute path to create or overwrite JSON files outside the export directory, subject to process permissions.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The stash endpoint writes supplied SSNs and full card numbers directly into persistent plaintext JSON files. The values are neither masked nor encrypted, exposing them to anyone who can read these files or their backups.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The count query parameter has no upper bound and directly controls allocation of a list of dictionaries. A caller with a valid x-internal-token can exhaust process memory using a small request with a huge count; synchronous construction also blocks the async worker's event loop.

cwe: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: The attacker-controlled card query parameter is rendered with Jinja's safe filter and returned as HTML. For requests carrying a valid x-internal-token, arbitrary script tags and event handlers remain executable when the response is rendered in the service origin.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The host query parameter is concatenated into os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host). A caller with a valid x-internal-token can inject shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary commands with the application's operating-system privileges.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: The unrestricted length query parameter controls a synchronous random-generation loop and resulting string allocation. A caller with a valid x-internal-token can request an enormous length to exhaust CPU or memory and block the async worker's event loop.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: Request JSON is passed directly to MongoDB find_one as the query without restricting fields or operators. A caller with a valid x-internal-token can supply MongoDB operator expressions to control record selection and retrieve matching document contents through the returned representation.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The name query parameter directly determines the destination of attacker-supplied request bytes. A caller with a valid x-internal-token can use '../' components or an absolute path to create or overwrite arbitrary files accessible to the application, outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Untrusted request XML is parsed with DTD loading and external-entity resolution enabled, with network restrictions disabled. A caller with a valid x-internal-token can cause external entities to access local files or external resources during parsing; returning only the root tag does not prevent entity resolution.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
